title_zh: 是我爱她，也是我看错了
deck_zh: 承认这份爱是我的，不是说她属于我。它有时只从一件很小的事显出来：把几封信重新读过，终于承认，那一判是自己下的。
deck_en: Calling a love mine does not make the other person mine. Sometimes the distinction becomes visible in a much smaller admission: I was the one who read those messages that way.
body_zh: 她是兽医，他做城市规划。他们认识快一年了。他爱她，却说不准她知不知道。有一个月，她回信慢了，字少了，语气也客客气气。他把那几封信看了又看，越看越像一件事：她在疏远他。
他想起上次聚会，自己当着朋友的面说过一句不得体的话。大概从那以后，她就看轻了他。他给老朋友写信，说她就是这样，热一阵冷一阵，是她让自己会错了意。后来他才知道，那个月她母亲住院，她白天看诊，晚上守病房，短信是在走廊里匆匆打的。
他又读了一遍，脸红了。原来不是那些字已经把意思说定，是他从那些字里读出了一个意思。是我看错了。这一回，错没有再被推出去。
这不是什么爱情的升级仪式。一个人可以突然被一个声音牵动，也可以在同一份爱里意识到“是我爱她”。这里看的是后一面：不是她把一份爱塞进我手里，也不是命运替我承担。来处未必由我选择，这份爱却是我的。
## 那一判是谁下的
爱有了主人，容易被听成爱终于有了主宰。恰好不是。他不能因为承认自己爱她，就命令这份爱立刻开始、立刻停止，更没有因此取得她的所有权。“我的爱”与“我的人”，并不是同一句话。
这里的主人很小，小到只是一个错误能够回来的地方。他觉得一切都对时，像是世界本来如此：她的冷淡明明白白，自己的委屈理所当然。等发现读错了，才看见这个判断原来有人下过。那个人是自己。
假如她确实没有把事情告诉他呢？也许她不想让他担心，回信只说一切都好。这样，他看错就有她的一份缘由。可“她在疏远我”仍是他从短信中作出的判断，没有人替他读。她的隐瞒需要另看，不能用来把这一判转交给她；他承认自己看错，也没有让她那一份凭空消失。
把事情认回自己，不是把所有责任全揽到身上。不是“都是我不好”，更不是“我根本不配爱人”。这些话听起来也朝着自己，却可能绕开了具体的那一次看错，转而给整个人判刑。要看清的只是：我怎样从那几句话走到了那个结论。
旁人也不能仅凭一句“是你让我误会”，便断言说话的人从未反省。人可以嘴上推开，心里已经转过来；也可以把认错的话说得很漂亮，里面仍在责怪对方。我们听得见话，不能因此看穿那一下有没有发生。
他没有立刻向她作一番郑重的检讨，只是把信又读了一遍，那一下也可以是真的。若后来告诉她“我原来把你的忙当成了冷淡”，这句话又成了一次新的来往；它怎样到达她那里，需要另看。认出自己的错误，不必等一场被别人验收的仪式。
她也在看他。那个月，他的信一封比一封长，她也许觉得，他只顾自己的感受。可她也可能看错：他反复追问，是因为害怕。被爱的人不只是一个被注视的样子，她同样会判断，会误解，也会重新考虑。
后来两个人说开，他讲自己怎么误读，她讲自己当时怎么想。各人的错误，仍得各自认回来。他能告诉她她看漏了什么，不能替她认；她也不能替他改。给出自己的理解，而不把对方该怎样理解一并写好，谈话才可能留下空间。
## 她不是一面替我照好的镜子
在一起以后，他发现自己也喜欢爱着她的那个自己：细心，耐得住，知道等。这个发现本身没有错。被喜欢的人看见，本来就是亲近的一部分。盼她知道自己曾经慌过，也不等于在控制她。
可有时，事情会慢慢掉个头。他问：“你说，我是不是很懂你？”她说有些地方懂，有些地方未必。他并不想听后半句，再问一次，直到她笑着答是。原本想被看见，变成了要求她必须照出一个事先定好的自己。
“我是不是懂你”，可以只是一个问题。她说不是，也仍算一个回答，这一问就还开着。问得勤、少答一天便不安，也不能单独证明他在接管她。差别在于，他究竟有没有让她的回答可以不是自己预先想好的那句。
“你还爱我吗”也一样。它能是一句脆弱的追问，不必被判成坏话。可若每次只许有一个答案，不许不答，不许另答，连迟疑都要被纠正，她的回应就被安排成了一面镜子，用来证明那个被爱着的我还在。
这时要分清：我爱她，顺带喜欢爱着她的自己；我爱的恰好是那个被她确认的自己。后者看起来也处处有一个“我”，却不再是错误能回来的地方，而是一个不许照出别的样子的形象。她的眼睛，渐渐被要求替这个形象工作。
她后来是否真的只照着他的需要回答，是另一件事。一次要求朝替人决定的方向去了，不等于它已经占住了她的理解。她可能拒绝，也可能指出这个要求。要看她以后的理解与行动，不能只从他问过几次就宣布一切已经发生。
还有一种情形，更容易和爱情混在一起。朋友刚分手，急着再找一个人。谁对他好，他就往谁那里去；来的是谁不要紧，要紧的是自己又在恋爱。他先爱上了“在爱着”，再找人把那个位置填上。
奥古斯丁回看年轻的自己时，已经认出过先爱上爱、再寻找可爱对象的样子。但想恋爱，也不自动证明任何人都可以替换。要问的是眼前这个人究竟还算不算这一个，而不是只凭寂寞或热烈替人下结论。
心里的那个故事，还不等于已经对别人做了什么。一个人想象自己会被爱情拯救，先是他与自己的事；当他说“你就是来救我的，你该陪我把上一段的伤养好”，把角色交给另一个人照着演，才开始进入那个人的生活。镜子在自己这里，要她来照，是后来的一步。
这也不是给人贴一个“自恋”的标签。弗洛伊德曾讨论，人可能在所爱者身上爱自己的样子、过去或理想，那是在追问对象选择的来路。这里不凭来路判人，只看这一次：她的看法，是否仍然可以是她的看法。
## 说不全，仍然是我爱她
问他为什么爱她，他说她给受伤的猫处理伤口时手很稳，说她说话慢，想清楚才开口。说了几样，自己也知道不是全部。承认爱是自己的，不表示同时掌握了它的全部来历，知道每一种声音为什么恰好能牵动自己。
他怎样长大、见过谁、什么时候学会害怕失去，有些不是他选择的。认识到这份爱是我的，并不会使这些来处突然透明。说不全，不必被当成敷衍，也不必靠一套完整的理由才能获得爱的资格。
后来他打趣说，我们大概上辈子就认识。可以这样说，作为今天回看的一种说法；它不必被赶出诗意。只是这句话不是当初那一下的组成，更不能替当下的人承担。如果“命中注定”意味着自己的判断再不用面对，就又把主人推开了；若变成“你注定属于我”，更已经替她写了去处。
几年以后，他或许还会发现，自己爱着的有一部分是想象里的她：永远镇定，总在自己需要时出现。真的她会慌，会累，会在医院走廊只回几个字。那一部分想象结束，不必把余下的爱也一并判成虚假。看清了，仍然可能爱。
也可能有一份依着误解而生的爱，真的在看清时结束了。说“原来是我看错”，与要求她承认“是你骗我爱你”，是两种不同的面对。她真瞒过什么，已有的承诺与依靠又留下什么，都仍须分别看，不能靠一种结束替所有事情结账。
甚至看错的转身，也可能发生在爱情之前。一个人先发现自己太快地下了结论，才第一次给另一个人让出被重新看见的地方。承认误解，不等于已经爱了，却可能不再让旧判断挡在门口。
这一篇没有给出更会爱的人应该长什么样。它只留下一个很小、也并不容易的区别：我可以承认，牵动我的不是我安排好的；也可以承认，由那些牵动长出的判断，不是别人替我下的。是我爱她，正因为如此，她仍不是我的镜子。
body_en: She is a vet; he works in urban planning. They have known each other for almost a year. He loves her, though he is not sure she knows it. Then, for a month, her messages grow shorter. Replies take days. They sound polite, almost formal. He reads them repeatedly and arrives at an explanation: she is withdrawing.

He remembers saying something awkward in front of friends. Perhaps she has thought less of him ever since. In a letter to an old friend he calls her inconsistent, warm one moment and cold the next. He writes that she has made him misunderstand. Only later does he learn that her mother was in hospital. She worked at the clinic by day and stayed at the bedside at night, answering on her phone in the corridor.

He reads the messages again and blushes. The meaning had not simply been lying there. He had read a meaning into them. I got this wrong. Something that had been placed entirely on her side returns to his.

This is not a promotion to a more advanced kind of love. Being caught by someone’s voice and recognizing that the love is mine can be aspects of the same experience. Here we follow the second: whatever brought this love about, it is not something she must own for me, nor something fate can take responsibility for.
## The judgment comes back to someone

To call the love mine is not to call her mine. Nor does it make me its master, able to start or stop it on command. The ownership at issue is much smaller: there is someone to whom a mistaken judgment can return.

When everything seems obvious, that someone is easy to miss. Her coldness appears to announce itself; my resentment seems simply to follow the facts. Error exposes the missing step. Someone had to move from those brief messages to the conclusion that she no longer cared. That person was me.

Suppose she really withheld information. Perhaps she did not want him to worry and wrote that everything was fine. Her silence would then be part of the explanation for his mistake. It would not make the interpretation hers. What she concealed and what he concluded are separate matters; acknowledging either one does not cancel the other.

Taking back a judgment is not taking the blame for everything. ‘I am terrible; I should never love anyone’ may sound self-directed while avoiding the particular mistake altogether. It replaces an inquiry into how I read those messages with a verdict on my entire person. The smaller admission need not be a trial of the self.

An observer also has limits. Hearing him say that she made him misunderstand does not establish that no reconsideration took place within him. He might blame her aloud while recognizing his own part privately. He might apologize beautifully while refusing to reconsider. Words offer evidence; they do not open the whole inner event to inspection.

He need not conduct a ceremonial confession before the recognition counts. Reading the messages again may be enough for that inward turn. Telling her would be a further event: his words would enter her circumstances and invite a response. The two should not be confused.

She is looking at him too. During that month his messages become longer and more insistent. She may conclude that he thinks only of himself. She may also be wrong: the insistence may come from fear. The person loved is not merely a figure in someone else’s field of vision. She makes judgments, can misread, and can reconsider.

Later they discuss the month. Each explains a misunderstanding. Neither can perform the other’s recognition or revision. He can offer what she missed without prescribing how she must now understand him. That difference is part of what can leave a conversation open.
## Wanting to be seen, requiring a reflection

Once they are together, he discovers that he likes himself in love: attentive, patient, willing to wait. Nothing about that discovery is automatically objectionable. Wanting the person one loves to see one’s care belongs to closeness. Hoping she understands how frightened he was need not make her a mirror.

But the arrangement can turn around. He asks whether he understands her well. She says that he does in some ways, not in others. The second half is unwelcome. He asks again until she gives the answer he wanted. Being seen has become a demand to be reflected in an image prepared beforehand.

The question itself need not do this. If ‘Not entirely’ can remain an answer, the exchange is still open. Nor can frequency or anxiety settle the issue. Asking often, or feeling unsettled when she does not reply, does not by itself prove that he is taking over her part. The question is whether her answer is allowed to differ from his script.

‘Do you still love me?’ can likewise be a vulnerable question. It changes when every response must provide the same reassurance, when silence or hesitation must be corrected, and when her reply is assigned the job of establishing who he is. She is no longer simply being asked. Her looking is being made to service his image of himself as loved.

Two things need separating: loving her and also liking the person I become in loving her; loving, above all, that agreeable person she is required to confirm. The latter contains plenty of talk about the self. It need not contain the modest self to which an error can return.

An attempt to fix her response is not proof that it has succeeded. She might refuse, name the demand, or answer differently. What the action becomes in her understanding and subsequent conduct is not decided by counting how often he asked. The direction of an act and its completion at the other end are different questions.

Another friend has just separated and urgently wants to fall in love again. Anyone kind enough seems a possible candidate. The important thing is to be in love; who arrives matters less. Augustine recognized something resembling this wish to love before there is a particular beloved. Yet wanting love does not automatically make everyone interchangeable. That further question must still be asked.

A private fantasy also differs from an interpersonal demand. Imagining that romance will rescue me is initially something happening at my end. Telling someone that they have come to save me and must heal the previous relationship assigns them a part to perform. Only when the fantasy enters their life through words or actions do we read what it is doing toward them.

None of this supplies a diagnosis of narcissism. Freud investigated ways in which people may love their present, former, or ideal selves in another person; that is an inquiry into the origins of attachment. Here we do not classify a person from those origins. We ask what happens in this encounter: can her view still be hers?
## The love can be mine without being fully explained

Ask him why he loves her. He mentions the steadiness of her hands treating an injured cat, the way she pauses before speaking. He can name things. He also knows that the list is not complete. Recognizing the love as his does not make its entire history transparent.

How he grew up, whom he met, what taught him to fear losing someone: much of that was not chosen. Acknowledgment does not erase those conditions. Nor does an incomplete explanation disqualify a love. Being unable to give every reason need not be evasion or a shortage of sincerity.

Later he jokes that they must have known each other in a previous life. A retrospective story can have poetry without becoming the cause of the original encounter. If destiny means that he no longer has to own his judgments, it moves the speaker out of the picture. If it becomes ‘You were destined to be mine,’ it also begins writing her future for her.

Years later he may see that part of his love concerned an imagined woman: always calm, always available when needed. The actual woman gets frightened, tired, and sometimes sends only a few words from a hospital corridor. That imagined part can end without making every remaining part false. Seeing more clearly need not mean ceasing to love.

A love dependent on a misreading may also genuinely end. ‘I misunderstood’ and ‘You must admit that you deceived me into loving you’ meet that ending differently. Any actual concealment remains a separate matter. So do promises and reliance already established. An ending cannot settle them all by changing the account.

The turn can even precede love. Someone discovers that they judged too quickly and becomes able to see a person they had dismissed. Correcting a judgment is not already falling in love. It can remove something that prevented a meeting.

There is no portrait here of the person who has finally learned to love properly. There is a smaller distinction. I can acknowledge that the original attraction was not mine to arrange, while admitting that the judgments formed around it were not made for me by someone else. The love is mine. For that very reason, she need not become its mirror.
